subproblems.title: Mass upper bound for a current represented by a unit-bounded multivector field
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), let μ be a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^P, and let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n, the continuous linear functionals on n-covectors). Write |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. Assume:
- |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every x ∈ ℝ^P and every n-covector α;
- T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n). This is a Bochner integral, equal to 0 when the integrand is not μ-integrable.
Then M_W(T) = T.massOn W ≤ μ(W) for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), T.massOn W ≤ μ W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (upper bound) of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_const_vector_massOn, written for a variable unit-bounded field ξ and a general measure μ. The parent applies it to the constant field ξ ≡ s⁻¹ζ₀ and μ = ofReal(s)·ν, so the supplied pointwise bound |ζ₀(ω(x))| ≤ s·1_{tsupport ω}(x) becomes |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ 1_{tsupport ω}(x). This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem cmrc_massOn_le_of_repr; its frozen type is reused verbatim.
Notation. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. For r ∈ ℝ, ofReal r ∈ [0, ∞]. ‖r‖ₑ = ofReal|r| is the extended norm of r ∈ ℝ. 1_K is the indicator function of K.
1. (Reduction.) By definition (Simon 6.2.5; GeometricCurrentOn.massOn), M_W(T) is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. These are the ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P. By the least-upper-bound property (sSup_le) it suffices to prove ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ μ(W) for one fixed admissible ω.
2. (Notation.) Put K := tsupport ω and f(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) ∈ ℝ. K is closed, hence Borel, and K ⊆ W. By hypothesis, T(ω) = ∫ f dμ.
3. (Pointwise bound.) If x ∈ K, then |f(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1, by the hypothesis on ξ and admissibility. If x ∉ K, then ω(x) = 0, since x lies outside the closed support of ω (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport); so f(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0 by linearity of ξ(x). Hence ‖f(x)‖ₑ ≤ 1_K(x) for every x.
4. (Integral bound.) ofReal(T(ω)) = ofReal(∫ f dμ) ≤ ofReal|∫ f dμ| = ‖∫ f dμ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ dμ. The last inequality (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm) holds for every function f. If f is μ-integrable it is the usual estimate; otherwise ∫ f dμ = 0 and the left side is 0. In particular, no measurability of ξ is needed.
5. By step 3 and monotonicity of the lower Lebesgue integral, ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ dμ ≤ ∫⁻ 1_K dμ = μ(K), since K is measurable (lintegral_indicator_one). Since K ⊆ W, μ(K) ≤ μ(W) by monotonicity of μ, which holds for arbitrary sets W.
6. Steps 4–5 give ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ μ(W) for every admissible ω. Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M_W(T) ≤ μ(W). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to ofReal(T ω) ≤ μ(W) for each ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W (sSup_le).
With K = tsupport ω and f(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)): |f| ≤ |ω| ≤ 1 on K and f = 0 off K, so ‖f‖ₑ ≤ 1_K.
ofReal(∫ f dμ) ≤ ‖∫ f dμ‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻ ‖f‖ₑ dμ ≤ μ(K) ≤ μ(W); the middle step holds for every f, so ξ needs no measurability.
Take the supremum over admissible ω.

subproblems.title: L¹ approximation of a unit-bounded covector field by unit test forms supported in an open set
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), IsFiniteMeasure ν → IsOpen V → ν Vᶜ = 0 → Integrable β ν → (∀ᵐ x ∂ν, covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - β x)) ∂ν < ENNReal.ofReal ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the cut-off/test-form construction behind steps 3–4 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_const_vector_massOn (unit forms supported in W that equal β on a large compact set), generalized from a constant β to an integrable unit-bounded field β, as the sibling norming_lower needs. This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem rsd_mw_exists_testForm_approx; its frozen type is reused verbatim.
Notation:
- F := Λⁿ(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖·‖. F is finite-dimensional, hence complete.
- N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
- 𝓘 := the set of strictly increasing I : {0, …, n−1} → {0, …, P−1}, and e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j).
- m := ν(ℝ^P) < ∞, regarded as a real number ≥ 0.
- 'a.e.' refers to ν.
1. (Properties of N.)
 - N(α) = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α(e_I)²)^{1/2} = ‖c(α)‖₂, where c : F → ℝ^𝓘, c(α) := (α(e_I))_{I∈𝓘}, is linear and ‖·‖₂ is the Euclidean norm.
 - Hence N ≥ 0, N(0) = 0, N(tα) = |t|·N(α) and N(α + α′) ≤ N(α) + N(α′).
 - Since |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_k‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, we get N(α) ≤ C‖α‖ with C := (#𝓘)^{1/2} ≥ 0.
 - Consequently |N(α) − N(α′)| ≤ N(α − α′) ≤ C‖α − α′‖, so N is continuous.
2. (Compact core.) For j ≥ 1 let K_j := {y : ‖y‖ ≤ j and B(y, 1/j) ⊆ V}, where B is the open ball.
 - For r > 0 the set {y : B(y, r) ⊆ V} is closed. Indeed, let y_k → y with B(y_k, r) ⊆ V, and let |z − y| < r; then |z − y_k| < r for large k, so z ∈ V.
 - Hence K_j is closed and bounded, so compact. Also K_j ⊆ V (as y ∈ B(y, 1/j)) and K_j ⊆ K_{j+1}.
 - ⋃_j K_j = V because V is open: if B(y, r) ⊆ V, take j ≥ max(‖y‖, 1/r).
 - The measurable sets V ∖ K_j decrease to ∅ and ν is finite, so ν(V ∖ K_j) → 0 (continuity from above, tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop).
 - Since ν(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, ν(ℝ^P ∖ K_j) ≤ ν(ℝ^P ∖ V) + ν(V ∖ K_j) = ν(V ∖ K_j).
 - Fix K := K_j with ν(ℝ^P ∖ K) < ofReal(ε/8).
3. (Continuous approximation.) ν is a finite Borel measure on the σ-compact, locally compact metric space ℝ^P, hence regular (Measure.Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). Continuous compactly supported maps are dense in L¹(ν; F) (Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le). So there is a continuous, compactly supported, ν-integrable g : ℝ^P → F with ∫‖g(x) − β(x)‖ dν(x) ≤ ε/(8(C + 1)).
4. (Radial retraction.) Define π : F → F by π(a) := max(1, N(a))⁻¹·a.
 - π is continuous (N is continuous and max(1, N) ≥ 1), π(0) = 0, and N(π(a)) = N(a)/max(1, N(a)) ≤ 1.
 - If N(b) ≤ 1, then N(π(a) − b) ≤ 2N(a − b). If N(a) ≤ 1 then π(a) = a. Otherwise π(a) = a/N(a) and N(a − π(a)) = (1 − 1/N(a))·N(a) = N(a) − 1 ≤ N(a) − N(b) ≤ N(a − b). So N(π(a) − b) ≤ N(π(a) − a) + N(a − b) ≤ 2N(a − b).
 - Put g₁ := π∘g. Then g₁ is continuous and compactly supported (g₁(x) = 0 whenever g(x) = 0), and N(g₁(x)) ≤ 1 for every x.
 - For a.e. x (namely where N(β(x)) ≤ 1), N(g₁(x) − β(x)) ≤ 2N(g(x) − β(x)) ≤ 2C‖g(x) − β(x)‖.
5. (Smoothing.) g₁ is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous. Let η := ε/(8(C + 1)(m + 1)) > 0. By UniformContinuous.exists_contDiff_dist_le (convolution with a smooth bump of small radius; ℝ^P is finite-dimensional and F is complete), there is a C^∞ map g₂′ : ℝ^P → F with ‖g₂′(x) − g₁(x)‖ < η for every x. Put g₂ := (1 + Cη)⁻¹·g₂′, which is also C^∞.
 - N(g₂′(x)) ≤ N(g₁(x)) + N(g₂′(x) − g₁(x)) ≤ 1 + Cη, so N(g₂(x)) ≤ 1 for every x.
 - g₂′(x) − g₂(x) = (Cη/(1 + Cη))·g₂′(x). So N(g₂(x) − g₁(x)) ≤ (Cη/(1 + Cη))·N(g₂′(x)) + N(g₂′(x) − g₁(x)) ≤ Cη + Cη = 2Cη.
6. (Smooth cut-off.) K is compact, V is open and K ⊆ V in the locally compact Hausdorff space ℝ^P.
 - There is an open V₀ with K ⊆ V₀, closure V₀ compact and closure V₀ ⊆ V (exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure).
 - The smooth Urysohn lemma (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff, for the open set V₀ and the closed set K ⊆ V₀) gives a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with support χ = V₀ and χ = 1 on K.
 - Then tsupport χ = closure V₀ is compact and contained in V.
 - Define ω(x) := χ(x)·g₂(x). Then ω is C^∞, as the product of a C^∞ scalar function and a C^∞ F-valued map.
 - tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ V, and ω has compact support. So IsTestForm ω and tsupport ω ⊆ V.
 - N(ω(x)) = χ(x)·N(g₂(x)) ≤ 1 for every x.
7. (Estimate.) Let x satisfy N(β(x)) ≤ 1 and the inequality of step 4; a.e. x does.
 - If x ∈ K, then ω(x) = g₂(x), so N(ω(x) − β(x)) ≤ N(g₂(x) − g₁(x)) + N(g₁(x) − β(x)) ≤ 2Cη + 2C‖g(x) − β(x)‖.
 - If x ∉ K, then N(ω(x) − β(x)) ≤ N(ω(x)) + N(β(x)) ≤ 2.
 Hence, a.e., ofReal(N(ω(x) − β(x))) ≤ ofReal(2Cη) + ofReal(2C‖g(x) − β(x)‖) + 2·1_{ℝ^P∖K}(x). Integrate, using ν(ℝ^P) = m and ∫⁻ ofReal‖g − β‖ dν = ofReal ∫‖g − β‖ dν (g − β is integrable):
 ∫⁻ ofReal(N(ω − β)) dν ≤ ofReal(2Cηm) + ofReal(2C·∫‖g − β‖ dν) + 2ν(ℝ^P ∖ K).
 Bound each term:
 - 2Cηm = (ε/4)·(C/(C + 1))·(m/(m + 1)) ≤ ε/4;
 - 2C·∫‖g − β‖ dν ≤ (ε/4)·(C/(C + 1)) ≤ ε/4;
 - 2ν(ℝ^P ∖ K) < 2·ofReal(ε/8) = ofReal(ε/4).
 So ∫⁻ ofReal(N(ω − β)) dν < ofReal(3ε/4) ≤ ofReal ε.
Thus ω has all the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: covectorEuclideanNorm N is a continuous seminorm with N ≤ C‖·‖.
Compact K ⊆ V with ν(ℝ^P ∖ K) < ε/8, by a compact exhaustion of V and continuity from above.
An L¹-close continuous compactly supported g; the radial retraction π gives N(π∘g) ≤ 1 and N(π∘g − β) ≤ 2C‖g − β‖ a.e.
A uniform C^∞ approximation, rescaled by (1 + Cη)⁻¹ to keep N ≤ 1, multiplied by a smooth Urysohn cut-off χ (χ = 1 on K, tsupport χ compact ⊆ V), gives a unit test form ω.
Split the error over K and ℝ^P ∖ K: ∫⁻ ofReal N(ω − β) dν < 3ε/4 < ε.

subproblems.title: Mass lower bound on compactly contained open sets from a norming covector field
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → AEStronglyMeasurable β μ → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x, ‖β x‖ ≤ C) → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ξ x (β x) = 1) → ∀ W W' : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W' → CompactlyContained W' U → W' ⊆ W → μ W' ≤ T.massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 (lower bound) of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_const_vector_massOn. M_W is tested against unit test forms supported in a compactly contained open W′ ⊆ W that approximate a norming covector field β. The supplied proof takes ω_j = φ_jβ for a constant β. For a general field β the cut-off product is replaced by the approximation of the sibling testform_approx. The parent applies this child with constant fields ξ ≡ s⁻¹ζ₀, β ≡ β₀ and μ = ofReal(s)·ν. This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem cmrc_measure_le_massOn_of_norming; its frozen type is reused verbatim.
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ν := μ restricted to W′ (μ.restrict W′).
1. (Finiteness.) closure W′ is compact and contained in U, so μ(W′) ≤ μ(closure W′) < ∞ by (i). Hence ν is a finite measure with ν(ℝ^P) = μ(W′). Moreover ν(W′ᶜ) = μ(W′ᶜ ∩ W′) = 0, since W′ᶜ is closed, hence measurable.
2. (β is ν-integrable.) β is ν-a.e. strongly measurable by (v), since restriction preserves a.e. strong measurability. Also ‖β(x)‖ ≤ C for all x by (vi), and ν is finite, so β is ν-integrable (Integrable.of_bound). By (vii), |β(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, in particular ν-a.e.
3. (Approximation.) Fix ε > 0. Apply the sibling testform_approx (rsd_mw_exists_testForm_approx) to P, n, ν, V := W′, β and ε. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1–2: ν is finite, W′ is open, ν(W′ᶜ) = 0, β is ν-integrable, and |β| ≤ 1 ν-a.e. It gives an n-form ω₀ with:
 - IsTestForm ω₀ and tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W′;
 - |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 for every x;
 - ∫⁻ ofReal|ω₀(x) − β(x)| dν(x) < ofReal ε.
4. (Admissibility.) tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W′ ⊆ closure W′ ⊆ U, so ω₀ defines an element ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) = TestFormOn U n. Moreover tsupport ω ⊆ W′ ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. So ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).
5. (Localization.) Put f(x) := ξ(x)(ω₀(x)). For x ∉ W′ we have x ∉ tsupport ω₀, so ω₀(x) = 0 and f(x) = 0. By (iv) and setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, T(ω) = ∫ f dμ = ∫_{W′} f dμ = ∫ f dν.
6. (Integrability.) f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: x ↦ (ξ(x), ω₀(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable by (ii) and continuity of ω₀, and evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous, being bounded bilinear. By (iii), |f(x)| ≤ |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Since ν is finite, f and the constant 1 are ν-integrable.
7. (Pointwise lower bound.) Let h := 1 − f; then h ≥ 0 everywhere, since f ≤ 1. By (viii), ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 for μ-a.e. x, hence for ν-a.e. x (ν ≪ μ). For such x, linearity of ξ(x) and (iii) give f(x) = ξ(x)(β(x)) + ξ(x)(ω₀(x) − β(x)) = 1 + ξ(x)(ω₀(x) − β(x)) ≥ 1 − |ω₀(x) − β(x)|. That is, h(x) ≤ |ω₀(x) − β(x)| for ν-a.e. x.
8. (Integral of h.) h ≥ 0 and h is ν-a.e. strongly measurable, so ∫ h dν = (∫⁻ ofReal h dν).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae). By steps 7 and 3, ∫⁻ ofReal h dν ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal|ω₀ − β| dν < ofReal ε (lintegral_mono_ae). Hence ∫ h dν < ε (ENNReal.toReal_lt_of_lt_ofReal).
9. (Lower bound for T(ω).) By integral_sub and integral_const, ∫ h dν = ∫ 1 dν − ∫ f dν = μ.real(W′) − ∫ f dν, since ν(ℝ^P) = μ(W′). Therefore T(ω) = ∫ f dν = μ.real(W′) − ∫ h dν > μ.real(W′) − ε.
10. (Fixed ε.) μ(W′) = ofReal(μ.real W′), because μ(W′) < ∞. Hence, by ENNReal.ofReal_add_le and steps 9 and 4: μ(W′) ≤ ofReal(μ.real W′ − ε) + ofReal ε ≤ ofReal(T(ω)) + ofReal ε ≤ M_W(T) + ofReal ε.
11. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, μ(W′) ≤ M_W(T) (ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: ν := μ⌞W′ is finite (closure W′ is a compact subset of U), ν(W′ᶜ) = 0, and β is ν-integrable with |β| ≤ 1.
Sibling testform_approx gives a unit test form ω₀ with tsupport ω₀ ⊆ W′ and ∫⁻ ofReal|ω₀ − β| dν < ofReal ε; ω₀ is admissible for M_W(T).
T(ω₀) = ∫_{W′} ξ(ω₀) dμ, and ξ(ω₀) ≥ 1 − |ω₀ − β| ν-a.e., because ξ(β) = 1 a.e. and |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|.
Hence T(ω₀) > μ.real(W′) − ε, so μ(W′) ≤ M_W(T) + ε for every ε > 0, and μ(W′) ≤ M_W(T).

subproblems.title: Measure of an open set bounded via its compactly contained open subsets
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^P, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P be open with μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, and let m ∈ [0, ∞]. Suppose μ(W′) ≤ m for every open W′ ⊆ W with W′ ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained W′ U: closure W′ is compact and contained in U). Then μ(W) ≤ m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (m : ℝ≥0∞), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ W' : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W' → CompactlyContained W' U → W' ⊆ W → μ W' ≤ m) → μ W ≤ m
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the exhaustion and continuity-from-below part of steps 3–4 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_const_vector_massOn (K_j ↑ W, ν(K_j) ↑ ν(W)). The exhaustion here is by relatively compact open sets W′_j instead of compact sets K_j. It uses the extended distance infEDist, so the case where the complement below is empty (e.g. W = U = ℝ^P) needs no separate treatment. The parent applies it with U = ℝ^P. This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem cmrc_measure_le_of_compactlyContained; its frozen type is reused verbatim.
1. O := W ∩ U is open. Since W ⊆ O ∪ Uᶜ, μ(W) ≤ μ(O) + μ(Uᶜ) = μ(O), by monotonicity and subadditivity of μ (valid for all sets) and μ(Uᶜ) = 0.
2. For j ∈ ℕ define
 - W′_j := {y : ‖y‖ < j and (j+1)⁻¹ < infEDist(y, Oᶜ)},
 - F_j := {y : ‖y‖ ≤ j and (j+1)⁻¹ ≤ infEDist(y, Oᶜ)},
 where (j+1)⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞) is computed in [0, ∞].
3. W′_j is open and F_j is closed. The maps y ↦ ‖y‖ and y ↦ infEDist(y, Oᶜ) are continuous (continuous_infEDist). A strict inequality between continuous functions defines an open set (isOpen_lt), and a non-strict one a closed set (isClosed_le). Since W′_j ⊆ F_j, closure W′_j ⊆ F_j (closure_minimal).
4. F_j ⊆ closedBall(0, j), which is compact because ℝ^P is proper. So F_j and its closed subset closure W′_j are compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
5. F_j ⊆ O. If y ∈ F_j and y ∉ O, then y ∈ Oᶜ, so infEDist(y, Oᶜ) = 0 < (j+1)⁻¹ (infEDist_zero_of_mem), a contradiction.
6. Hence closure W′_j is compact and closure W′_j ⊆ O ⊆ U, i.e. W′_j ⊂⊂ U. Also W′_j ⊆ closure W′_j ⊆ O ⊆ W. By hypothesis, μ(W′_j) ≤ m for every j.
7. The sequence (W′_j) is increasing: for j ≤ k, ‖y‖ < j ≤ k and (k+1)⁻¹ ≤ (j+1)⁻¹.
8. ⋃_j W′_j = O. The inclusion ⊆ follows from steps 3 and 5. Conversely, let y ∈ O.
 - Oᶜ is closed and y ∉ Oᶜ = closure Oᶜ, so infEDist(y, Oᶜ) ≠ 0 (mem_closure_iff_infEDist_zero). It equals ∞ if Oᶜ = ∅.
 - Choose j₁ with (j₁)⁻¹ < infEDist(y, Oᶜ) (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt) and j₂ > ‖y‖ (exists_nat_gt). Put j := max(j₁, j₂).
 - Then ‖y‖ < j₂ ≤ j and (j+1)⁻¹ ≤ (j₁)⁻¹ < infEDist(y, Oᶜ), so y ∈ W′_j.
9. By continuity from below along the increasing sequence (Monotone.measure_iUnion), μ(O) = sup_j μ(W′_j) ≤ m. With step 1, μ(W) ≤ m. ∎
proof_key_steps: W′_j := {‖y‖ < j, infEDist(y, (W∩U)ᶜ) > (j+1)⁻¹} are open and increasing, have compact closures inside W ∩ U, and exhaust W ∩ U.
By hypothesis μ(W′_j) ≤ m; continuity from below gives μ(W ∩ U) = sup_j μ(W′_j) ≤ m.
